exposure: type of cesarean section (Non-elective lower uterine CS, Elective lower uterine CS, Non-elective classical CS)
outcome: type of opioid supplied on discharge
cohort: The study participants were 46 patients who underwent a cesarean section at a tertiary referral obstetric hospital in September 2022.
finding: Non-elective classical CS procedures were associated with significantly higher use of opioid pain medications compared to other types of CS.
mod_finding: Non-elective classical CS procedures had higher total morphine equivalent opioid use (245.7 mg) compared to non-elective lower uterine CS (92.4 mg) and elective lower uterine CS (60.1 mg).
